That said, planning is an important step in being prepared and ready for your adventure. Remember, the Monument can be very unforgiving, and its wild character should not be underestimated. And although overnight stays on the monument do not require a permit, free permits are available at any of the local Visitor Centers and are highly encouraged. The permit system can become crucial in the case of a search and rescue . Below are some best practices to keep in mind when recreating on the GSENM: It’s always a good idea to let people know your itinerary and when you expect be back Travel in groups rather than by yourself Before beginning any of your Monument adventures, make sure you've planned your way in, and planned your way out Know the extended weather forecast Carry extra clothing, blankets, food and water for emergencies Remember, cell phone coverage across the Monument is sparse if at all Plan Ahead and Prepare

The Safford Field Office—whose boundaries stretch from the Navajo Nation in the north to the international boundary with Mexico in the south—is responsible for stewardship of eight units within BLM’s National Landscape Conservation System, including the Gila Box Riparian National Conservation Area , six wilderness areas, including the world-renowned Aravaipa Canyon Wilderness and one wilderness study area. The Salmon River, Bitterroot, and Lemhi ranges offer remote solitude, endless hiking, fishing, hunting, and exploration opportunities. Hikers and nature lovers find scenic and rugged terrain in the isolated, often-overlooked Lemhi Range where elk, deer, mountain goats, moose and black bears are abundant. The Salmon River, nicknamed the River of No Return, meanders through the second-deepest gorge on the continent and is well-known for outstanding fishing for anadromous (ocean-going) steelhead, along with rainbow and cutthroat trout. Rafters enjoy scenic floating and fishing along the calmer stretches of the river near the town of Salmon or tackling challenging whitewater (Class I-IV) on the stretch of river west of North Fork, Idaho. It is also host to one of the world's most flamboyant Carnivals, a hotbed for samba music, and the heartland of the martial art capoeira. In February 2027, for the first time in decades, Salvador Carnival will take place at the same time as Festa de Iemanjá, the major festival in candomblé—a religion that fuses Catholicism with West African religions—making this an ideal time to visit the city. It was April 1857, and in the past decade hundreds of Black Marylanders had slipped off the farms and plantations where they were enslaved. The San Juan Islands National Monument encompasses approximately 1,000 acres of land spread across many of these rocks and islands and managed by the Department of the Interior's Bureau of Land Management. Drawing visitors from around the world, this is a landscape of unmatched contrasts, where forests seem to spring from gray rock and distant, snow-capped peaks provide the backdrop for sandy beaches. The San Juan Islands National Monument is a trove of scientific and historic treasures, a refuge for an array of wildlife, and a classroom for generations of Americans. On March 25, 2013, President Obama signed a proclamation to designate the San Juan Islands National Monument. The proclamation states that, "The protection of these lands in the San Juan Islands will maintain their historical and cultural significance and enhance their unique and varied natural and scientific resources, for the benefit of all Americans." Home to the region's tallest alpine mountain that rises from the floor of the Sonoran Desert, the monument also will protect sacred, archaeological and cultural sites, including an estimated 1,700 Native American petroglyphs. Featuring thirty miles of the world-famous Pacific Crest National Scenic Trail, the area is a favorite for camping, hiking, hunting, horseback riding, photography, wildlife viewing, and even skiing. Fresh evidence from Cameron Bancroft - the culprit of the ball-tampering in South Africa in 2018 - has heaped pressure on Australia captain Pat Cummins, former coach Darren Lehmann and Cricket Australia. In a detailed account of more than 4,000 words published in the West Australian newspaper, Bancroft alleges all the Australia players and coaches present in Cape Town eight years ago knew of the plot. Bancroft's explosive testimony supports claims made by Usman Khawaja, David Warner and Chadd Sayers. However, Cummins denied Khawaja's version of events in his own extraordinary news conference in Sydney last week. Cummins spoke to the media for 68 minutes in an address broadcast on live television. Here, BBC Sport collects the most recent accounts of players and coaches involved in the saga that became widely known as sandpapergate. Usman Khawaja Batter Khawaja played all four Tests in South Africa and a total of 88 for Australia before retiring from international cricket earlier this year. Revelations in his autobiography reignited debate around the sandpaper scandal and made headlines across the globe.

The reason is simple to me. The very notion that Cameron Bancroft - the most inexperienced batsman in the Australia team at the time – would use sandpaper on the ball against South Africa without the bowlers knowing has never made sense. It has never seemed remotely plausible to me, as a former bowler, that the bowlers didn't know what was happening in Cape Town in 2018. It just doesn't seem possible. Therefore, this day of reckoning was always going to come. Let's be clear - as long as there has been cricket, there has been ball-tampering. There is no point hiding from the fact. Back in the day it was about shining the ball, maybe using something like a sweet to get a sheen on one side. Reverse swing was a ball-tampering game-changer. There was a requirement for a wearing process, roughing up and drying the ball. But, to get one thing straight, whether a ball is being tampered with or not, it belongs to the bowlers. pages.text: Sandpapergate: Usman Khawaja claims whole Australia team knew about use of sandpaper to tamper with ball against South Africa - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Usman Khawaja made his Test debut for Australia against England in 2011 By Timothy Abraham BBC Sport Journalist Published 6 November 2026 Usman Khawaja has claimed the entire Australia team knew about the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball in the final Test of their 2018 series with South Africa. In extracts of his autobiography - Sabr - published in the Sydney Morning Herald, , external the former opening batter said Australia had also used the ball-tampering tactic in the Test before the infamous match in Cape Town. The incident - nicknamed 'sandpapergate' - was widely condemned and led to bans for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft. "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," Khawaja, 39, told the Sydney Morning Herald. The four Australia bowlers who played in that match, including current Test captain Pat Cummins, have consistently denied they had any prior knowledge of the plan. Providing a picturesque backdrop to local communities, visitors can enjoy magnificent palm oases, snow-capped mountains, a national scenic trail, and wilderness areas. Its extensive backcountry can be accessed via trails from both the Coachella Valley and the alpine village of Idyllwild. Jointly managed by the BLM and the U.S. Forest Service, the Monument’s boundary encompasses about 280,000 acres, including public lands within the BLM’s California Desert Conservation Area and the San Jacinto Ranger District of the San Bernardino National Forest. The Monument includes two Federal wilderness areas -- the Santa Rosa and the San Jacinto. The Monument was established by an Act of Congress on October 24, 2000, "in order to preserve the nationally significant biological, cultural, recreational, geological, educational, and scientific values found in the Santa Rosa and San Jacinto Mountains" (Public Law 106-351). pages.text: Santander, Spain: A 2027 Guide to Its Waterfront Art Museums | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Beloved by Spaniards, Santander Is Becoming a Global Art Mecca The easygoing beachfront city is getting a host of new and reborn museums. A 2014 transformation by landscape architect Fernando Caruncho more than doubled the size of Pereda Gardens, in the historic heart of Santander. Luis Fonseca, Getty Images By Eddi Fiegel Published October 20, 2026 Santander, a port city in northwestern Spain, has long seduced Spaniards with its spectacular horseshoe bay surrounded by rolling green hills and the Cantabrian mountains in the distance. But now the city, the capital of the Cantabria region, is poised to become an international art destination. In September 2026, the new arts, culture, and technology center Faro Santander opened in a historic building redesigned by acclaimed British architect David Chipperfield with a permanent collection including works by such legendary figures as el Greco, Rubens, Velázquez, and Goya. ( See all 25 of the destinations that made our list of the best places to visit in 2027. ) Meanwhile, 2027 will bring the first outpost of Madrid’s renowned Reina Sofía museum. The impressive Museum of Prehistory and Archaeology of Cantabria also has a new home designed by the Barcelona-based architecture practice Mendoza Partida. Art lovers are sure to appreciate the city’s walkable city center—where ornate, neoclassical façades sit alongside Baroque churches and grand, porticoed squares—and the wide sandy beaches lined with elegant fin-de-siècle villas.

pages.text: Saracens: Canada captain Sophie De Goede signs new Saracens deal - BBC Sport Image source, Shutterstock Published 18 November 2026 Former World Player of the Year Sophie De Goede has signed a new one-year deal with Saracens. The 27-year-old back-row forward has had three spells with Sarries since 2020 and played 44 times for the club, most recently helping them claim the Premiership Women's Rugby title with victory over Trailfinders in June to make it a league and cup double. The World Rugby Player of the Year and member of World Rugby's Dream XV in 2025-26 captained Canada to the World Cup Final where they lost to England at Twickenham in 2025. "This club has been instrumental in supporting my development over my entire professional career to date. I feel very lucky to have the chance to echo Saracens' loyally to me back to the club," De Goede told the club website. , external Director of Rugby Alex Austerberry added: "Securing the long term-services of the 25-26 World Rugby Player of the Year is huge for the club and illustrates the desire of the club to remain at the forefront of the women's game. "Since returning from injury, which saw her miss the entirety of the 2024-25 season, Sophie's game has hit new heights both on the international stage and in club colours. pages.description: England head coach Sarina Wiegman has changed women's football in the country, so what does she face after signing a contract extension?
pages.text: Sarina Wiegman contract: Why England manager faces biggest challenge yet - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Sarina Wiegman has won the past three Women's European Championships - with the Netherlands in 2017 and England in 2022 and 2025 By Joe Bradshaw BBC Sport senior journalist Published 19 October 2026 When Sarina Wiegman took the reins as England manager in September 2021, she declared she had "come to bring the next level". Winner of the 2017 Women's Euros with her own Netherlands and runner-up at the subsequent World Cup in 2019, she certainly had the pedigree, but could she deliver on her promises? Five years on, Wiegman has pocketed two more European Championships and acquired another silver medal on the global stage. Not only that, but the success of her Lionesses exploded the women's game in this country, taking it not just to a new level, but to previously unthinkable heights. And yet on the day Wiegman extends her deal until after the Euros in 2029, her newest challenge could be her hardest yet. England manager Wiegman signs contract extension Published 19 October Why must England evolve? Wiegman's successful England teams have been built on a core group of players from an outstanding generation - but a few cracks have appeared this year. Seven of the team that started against world champions Spain in June also played in the Euro 2022 final against Germany - and their 4-0 defeat in Mallorca laid bare the gap England must bridge to the world's best. That result also consigned England to two rounds of play-offs to reach next summer's World Cup.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) manages the Trusted Traveler Programs. These include TSA Precheck and Global Entry . As a pre-approved member, you can use expedited lanes at U.S. airports and when entering the U.S. by land or sea. TSA Precheck is for travelers departing from U.S. airports. Global Entry is for travelers entering the U.S. from international destinations by air, land, or sea. There are also programs for entering the U.S. from Canada and Mexico. To apply, you will need to pay a fee and provide documents proving your identity. Depending on the program, you may need to complete an interview.
